findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the reports bucket are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption. Reporting data and the seeded vendor roster are persisted in cleartext at the storage layer, unlike the audit bucket which does use a KMS key.

The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger data is written unencrypted. This is the most sensitive dataset in the file and it receives weaker protection than the audit log bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set for the model artifacts bucket. Model artifacts (and any embedded training data or parameters) are stored without encryption at rest.

The runbooks bucket defines no server-side encryption. Operational runbooks commonly contain hostnames, escalation procedures, and occasionally embedded credentials or recovery keys, and are stored here unencrypted.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, and unlike the other buckets it does not even set an explicit private ACL. Any subsequent ACL or bucket policy granting public read would take effect unimpeded, exposing the archived reports and seeded vendor roster.

The bucket relies solely on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guardrail, so a later policy or ACL change (or an object written with a public ACL) could publicly expose financial ledger exports.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, removing the account-level defence-in-depth control against accidental public exposure of model artifacts.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so nothing prevents a public ACL or bucket policy from exposing internal operational runbooks.

The audit log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block. Publicly exposed access logs leak request patterns, object keys, and source IPs, and the bucket's log-delivery-write ACL already widens write access, so the block is especially important here.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party contact or commercial data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that itself has no default encryption, so the object is stored in cleartext.

Unlike model_artifacts, this bucket sends no server access logs to the audit_trail bucket, so reads and writes of financial ledger exports leave no independent access trail for detecting or investigating unauthorised access.
No logging block directs S3 server access logs to the audit_trail bucket, leaving accesses to archived reports and the seeded vendor roster unrecorded.
